items: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. It can be solids, liquids, or gases. Matter is made up of tiny particles called atoms and molecules.

blocks.text: Based on the composition, matter can be classified as:

items: 1. *Pure Substances:* Pure substances are substances that are made up of only one kind of particle and have a **fixed or constant structure**. *E.g. Diamond, sulphur, tin, etc.*
1. __*Element:*__ A pure substance made up of only **one type of atom** that **cannot** be broken down into **simpler substance** by chemical means. *E.g. H (Hydrogen) and O (Oxygen).*

2. __*Compound:*__ A pure substance made up of **two or more different types of elements** that are **chemically bonded** together in a fixed ratio. Elements can be separated into constituents by chemical or electrochemical change. *E.g. H2O (Water).*
2. __*Impure Substances:*__ Impure substances, also known as mixtures, are made up of two or more different substances. *E.g. Brass (Cu+Zn), Bronze (Cu+Sn).*
They have **distinct boundaries** and **fixed volumes**.
They have a **definite shape**.
They have a tendency to maintain the shape when subjected to outside force.
*Types of solids:* **Amorphous solids** and **Crystalline solids**.

Anisotropic in nature (properties vary with direction)
They have an irregular arrangement of constituent particles
They have a regular arrangement of constituent particles
They do not have sharp melting point

It can be produced in laboratory by **heating a gas** to an **extremely high temperature**.

items: The *fifth* state of matter is **Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC)**.
It is typically formed when a **gas of bosons** at very **low densities is cooled to temperatures very close to absolute zero**, i.e., *0 K (-273.15 C; -459.67 F)*.
*Origin of Name:* The term **"Boson"** comes from the name of **Dr. Satyendra Nath Bose**, an Indian physicist whose work on quantum mechanics was extended by **Albert Einstein** in **1925**.
*Discovery:* Dr. Bose published a research paper in **1924** and sent it to Einstein, who further developed the concept and predicted the existence of BEC in **1925**.
**1995: Eric Cornell** and **Carl Wieman** experimentally produced the first **BEC condensate** in a rarefied **gas of rubidium atoms** at extremely low temperature.
**1995: Wolfgang Ketterle** later created a BEC condensate with **sodium atoms. All three of them received Nobel Prize in Physics in 2001**.
__*Sublimation:*__ The process of changing a **solid directly into a gas** without passing through a liquid state. *E.g. Naphthalene, dry ice, etc.*

items: __*Deposition:*__ The opposite of sublimation, where a **gas turns into a solid without passing through a liquid state**. *E.g. The formation of frost or ice-crystals on the surface.*
__*Evaporation:*__ The process of changing a **liquid into a vapour by heating**. This happens at boiling point of liquid. *E.g. Evaporation of nail polish remover.*
__*Condensation:*__ The process by which **water vapour in air changes into liquid**. *E.g. Dew, Fog.*
When temperature **increases**, the rate **of evaporation increases**.
When surface area **increases**, the rate of **evaporation increases**.
When wind speed **increases**, the rate of **evaporation increases**.
When humidity **increases**, the rate of **evaporation decreases**.
A mixture is a composition of **two or more pure substances**.
Mixtures are considered to be **homogeneous** or **heterogeneous** in nature.

items: A solution is a homogeneous mixture formed when one or more substances **(solute)** dissolve in another substance **(solvent)**. The composition is uniform throughout, meaning the solute is evenly distributed within the solvent. *E.g.*
*Liquid into liquid: Water and Ink.*
*Solid into Solid: Alloys.*
*Gas into Gas: Air.*
*Solid into a liquid: Sugar and Water.*
*Gas into Solid: Hydrogen dissolved in palladium.*
*Gas into Liquid: Carbon Dioxide dissolved in water.*

items: 1. It is **homogeneous** in nature.
2. The particles of solution are too **small (less than 1 nm)**.
3. It **does not** scatter light.
4. It cannot be separated by filtration.

A solution of sugar in water is a solid in **liquid solution**. In this solution, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent.
A solution of iodine in alcohol known as **"Tincture of Iodine"**, this solution has iodine (solid) as the solute and alcohol (liquid) as the solvent. This solution is also used as **Antiseptic**.
Aerated drinks like soda water, etc., are gas in **liquid solutions**. These contain carbon dioxide (gas) as solute and water (liquid) as solvent.

Air is a mixture of gas in gas. Air is a **homogeneous mixture** of a number of gases. Its two main constituents are: oxygen (21%) and nitrogen (78%). The other gases are present in very small quantities.
1. __*Unsaturated Solution:*__ It is a solution that contains **less solute than the maximum amount it can dissolve**.
2. __*Saturated Solution:*__ It is a solution that contains the **maximum amount of solute that can dissolve** in a given amount of solvent at a specific temperature.
3. __*Concentrated Solution:*__ It contains a **large amount of solute relative to the solvent**.

items: A suspension is a mixture in which two or more substances are combined in a **non-uniform** manner. In a suspension, the **solute does not dissolve completely in the solvent**, and its particles remain large enough to be seen with naked eye. *E.g. Suspension may include muddy water, flour in water, and chalk powder in water.*
It is **heterogeneous** in nature.
It **scatters light** (shows Tyndall Effect) because particle size is large **(greater than 1000 nm)**.
It can be separated using **filtration method**.
It is **unstable** because solute gets settled down in solvent.

A colloid is a mixture in which one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another. Although colloids appear uniform (homogeneous) to the naked eye, they are actually **heterogeneous** when viewed under a microscope.
The particle size of colloid is intermediate **(1-1000 nm)** between that of a **solution** and **suspension**.

items: Colloids are **heterogeneous** in nature.
The particles **cannot** be seen through naked eyes **(particle size: Between 1 and 1000 nm)**.
The particles of **colloid do not settle** down if left uninterrupted, hence they are stable.
It cannot be separated through filtration method but can be separated through centrifugation.

When a beam of light is passed through a colloidal solution, the particles of the **colloid scatters the beam of light** and we can see the path of light in the solution. This is called as Tyndall Effect which was discovered in **1869**.

items: We can separate the **heterogeneous mixtures** into their constituents by means of physical methods such as -> **Filtration**, **Hand-picking**, **Sieving**.
__*Filtration:*__ It is a physical separation process that separates **solid matter** and **fluid from a mixture** using a filter medium.
__*Hand-picking:*__ It is a method of separating substances in a **mixture** by **hand** when the components are clearly visible enough to pick.
__*Sieving:*__ It is a method of using a **sieve** to distinguish small particles from bigger particles.

items: The law of Conservation of Mass states that in a closed system, the **total mass of a system remains constant** over time, meaning mass is neither created nor destroyed, but can only change form.

blocks.text: J.J. Thomson and Discovery of Electron (1897)
**1897:** J. J. Thomson performed **Cathode-Ray Experiment** by observing streams of particles emitted by cathode of a vacuum tube, which led to the discovery of the **electron**.

items: (i) An atom consists of a **positively charged sphere** and the **electrons are embedded** in it.
(ii) The negative and positive charges are **equal in magnitude**. So, the atom as a whole is electrically neutral.

**1904:** J. J. Thomson proposed the first atomic model, often referred to as the **"Plum Pudding Model"**, **"Raisin Pudding Model"**, or **"Watermelon Model"**. In this model, the **positive charge** is spread throughout the atom (like the bulk of pudding or watermelon), while the **electrons** are embedded within it (like plums or seeds).

items: In **1909**, Ernest Rutherford conducted the **Gold Foil Experiment** with the help of **Hans Geiger** and **Ernest Marsden**.
A few **α-particle** were deflected at small and large angles, indicating the presence of a dense, positively charged nucleus.

Rutherford used **gold foil** (about **1000** atoms thick) because gold is highly **malleable**, allowing it to be hammered into **ultra thin sheets**. A thicker foil would have prevented the **α-particle** from penetrating. The majority of alpha particles went through the gold foil without any deflection however a smaller number of alpha particles were slightly deflected from their original path. A very few **(1 in 8000)** were deflected backwards, at angles greater than 90°.
From the α-particles scattering experiment, Rutherford proposed the following atomic model:

items: (i) An atom has a **positively charged** centre, called the **nucleus**, where nearly all the atom's mass is concentrated.
(ii) **Electrons** revolve around the nucleus in **circular paths** (orbit).
(iii) The nucleus is **extremely small** compared to the overall size of the atom.
(iv) This experiment allowed him to estimate the relative
sizes of the different parts of the atom.

The atomic model failed to explain the distribution of electrons around the nucleus and the **stability of atoms**.
It did not explain why **atoms emit specific colour** when they are heated.
It failed to explain why different **elements react differently** or how **electrons are arranged**.
The atomic model **did not include energy levels** which was later explained through **Bohr's Model (1913)**.
In **1917**, Rutherford performed the **first artificially induced nuclear reaction** by conducting an experiment in which nitrogen nuclei was bombarded with α-particles.
Rutherford concluded that the **hydrogen** nucleus is a fundamental particle present in all atoms.
He named this positively charged particle the **proton (p)** in **1920**.

items: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in **stable orbits** (energy levels or shells) without losing energy in the form of radiation.
The orbits or energy levels are labeled **K, L, M, N**, with **K** being the **closest** to the nucleus and **N** being the **farthest**.
The **ground state is the lowest energy level** that an electron can occupy, typically referring to the electron's position in the K-shell (the innermost shell).
When an electron moves between different energy levels (or shells), it either **absorbs or emits energy**.
When an electron falls from a higher energy level to a lower one, it emits energy, usually in the form of electromagnetic radiation.
When an electron moves from a lower energy level to a higher one, it absorbs energy.
Bohr's model was groundbreaking but has a major limitation: it only works for one electron system, also called hydrogen-like species.
**Discrete Orbits:** Only certain special orbits known discrete orbits of electrons are allowed inside the atom.
**Energy Radiation:** While revolving in these discrete orbits, the electrons do not radiate energy.
**Wave-particle duality:** It was central to developing the Bohr model and, later the, full quantum mechanical model of the atom.

items: Alkynes generally have slightly *higher boiling point* than *alkenes* and *alkanes* (Alkyne > Alkene > Alkane) because of the stronger intermolecular forces arising from the triple bond.
Alkenes have stronger intermolecular forces than alkanes due to the double bond, so their bonding point is higher than that of alkanes, but lower than alkynes.
As the number of carbon in alkane increases, its boiling point increases significantly. Also, molecule with strong intermolecular forces will have high boiling points.
Solubility *decreases* as the length of hydrocarbon chain *increases*.
